page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine within the low-memory Dlsv7 general-purpose family. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz across 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, establishing a lean 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AMX-INT8, and AMX-TILE matrix accelerators, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression registering 34.6 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.78 GB/sec, placing both in the upper quartile. Standardized tests show average compute and memory throughput, including a PassMark CPU score of 8626.16, static web serving throughput of 8.6 GB/sec, and 8.2 million Redis SET operations per second. However, overall multi-core capacity remains constrained by the 4-vCPU envelope, as shown by lower-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (28.69 GB/sec) and weak medium-model LLM generation speeds.

The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures. In terms of cost efficiency, the reduced RAM-per-core ratio lowers infrastructure spend relative to standard memory configurations while providing modern enterprise CPU capabilities. Primary tradeoffs involve the absence of local ephemeral storage and limited parallel throughput under sustained multi-threaded execution.

Microsoft Azure D4ls_v7 is suitable for cost-conscious, compute-focused tasks that require high clock speeds without large memory allocations. Typical deployments include containerized web serving, batch compression, CI/CD worker nodes, API gateways, and lightweight edge inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v7 is an x86_64 cloud server provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Featuring 8.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation tailored for workloads that require modest memory capacity alongside high clock speeds. The processor incorporates modern vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance in compression routines, alongside average results in web serving and key-value operations. Multi-core compute performance is limited by the physical core count, and the instance provisions zero local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes. Because of its reduced memory profile and modern CPU architecture, D4ls_v7 is best suited for scale-out web serving, stateless microservices, batch data manipulation, and lightweight machine learning inference.
